raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Request for information on cost, impairment, and future guidance related to Best Egg transaction",
  "main_topics": ["Best Egg transaction", "costs", "impairment", "future guidance", "RoTE", "business growth"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": true,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "Starting with the Best Egg transaction, can you help us a bit on the cost and the impairment side of things? It's a day one integration cost and going forward, how would impairment flow through it? Presumably it's origination, so you don't have a lot of direct holding of the loan. So, does that mean impairment is also going to be quite low [versus revenues]? Number two, I know the 2028 target is something that you would not want to talk too much about right now. With the Best Egg transaction, we have greater visibility as to how we can get to mid-teens for the business, and then the UK businesses, all three of them are easily making greater than 20%. And if the Investment Bank is greater than 12% Group guidance for 2026, mechanically I think we can get quite close to 14%.",
  "answer_quote": "Okay, thank you Perlie. Let me take those in order. So the structure of Best Egg will be about $11 billion of what we call managed balances. Only about $1 billion we expect to be on the balance sheet. So therefore, the RWA position is relatively low and the direct impact of impairment is relatively low. So that's really what creates the stability of these returns and the relatively high RoTE of the business. So, I'm not going to give you specific numbers now on impairment, but expect it to be a relatively small number just because of the nature of the business model. As relates to costs, clearly, again we'll update you nearer to the time around our expectations on costs. A bit like what we did on Tesco. So, think no later than Q1, we'll give you a much fuller breakdown of what this is likely to look like. But we do expect some opportunities in the future to be able to generate cost synergies. In the immediate sort of short-term period we would expect to run this business somewhat standalone and then integrate it over time, a little bit like what we've done with the other smaller acquisitions. But I think what's really important here, and you can see it I guess from the numbers that we've given you, is that the RoTE of this business is extremely high. And even if you did it on an ROI basis, it remains high, and we expect to be able to grow that over time. On your second question, clearly I'm not going to give you a target now, but just remind you that when we set out the targets, RoTE, distributions, and the way we expect to grow our RWAs, 2026 was the only ever supposed to be a point in time and, and a sort of near term target. What you should be gleaning from us is that we are gaining momentum in the business, that we're gaining confidence in the business, and that's really what's led us to not only upgrade for the current year, but give you an indication that we're going to come to you a year before the current targets expire. But our ambition is to keep growing the returns of the business and really important for me, not just the returns, but the consistency and the stability of those returns. So more in February, I'm afraid. Thank you. Next question please."
}
